protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED recording hygiene, removal of a duplicate COORD heading
summary: Subject and prompt held. I counted the D-056 headings before reading the entry's claim, and there are exactly two — the only duplicated heading among seventy-one in the register. The important discovery is that the two blocks are not copies: 2825 bytes against 2406, each holding material the other lacks, so a plain deletion would lose content whichever one went. The entry saw that. Clause 3 unions the one sentence that is genuinely unique to the block being deleted, and I checked the rest by diffing the blocks myself: every other block-2 claim has a block-1 equivalent, most of them broader. The keep-the-first rationale is true and checkable, the deletion boundary matches the file's actual structure, and every claim in the union sentence is true of the adopted D-056 draft.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: c61c2590dfc9d586beb244db78bd8a244fdb1b7aa35d904f093a5809d07cfb58, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at d7b52f2e… across start and end.

The attack 'heading count is not actually two' fails, and I established the count independently before reading the entry so as not to be anchored by its claim. `## D-056 — Condition-2 SATISFIED versus qualification remainder` appears at lines 3343 and 3397, twice. A frequency sweep over all seventy-one `## D-nnn` headings in COORD returns D-056 as the only duplicate.

The two recitals are not duplicates in the sense the word usually carries, which is the fact that makes this entry non-trivial. Block one is 2825 bytes and block two 2406, and a line diff shows each contains material absent from the other. Block one carries the five Eligibility gates enumerated inline, the sentence 'D-013's SATISFIED-refusal stands until fixture authoring exists', and a four-condition readiness enumeration. Block two carries the eligible and ineligible row names and the D-002/D-010 deferral-limb sentence. Deleting either without care would drop something.

The attack 'deletes the wrong D-056 recital or both' fails. Clause 1 keeps exactly one, clause 2 deletes exactly one, and the stated reason for the choice is true: block one's readiness effect enumerates 'Condition 3 remains MET. Condition 4 remains PARTLY MET. Condition 5 remains NOT MET and last', and block two contains no such enumeration. The rejected alternative 'Delete the first and keep the second. Rejected: the first already enumerates conditions 2–5 standings; the second does not' is accurate.

The union in clause 3 covers exactly the gap, which I tested rather than took on trust. I extracted every substantive claim appearing in block two and checked each against block one: 'Execution remains condition 4 / DR-012' is present as 'Execution, QUALIFIED, and DEMONSTRATED remain condition 4 / DR-012'; 'D-015's design-contract recording stands' as 'D-015's recording of control-protocol-contract.v2 stands'; the live-cells point as the Eligibility gate 'MF-6 that records SATISFIED and removes the cell-level execution/measurement bar'; 'Does not rewrite D-001's five bullets' as 'rewrites none of D-001's five checklist bullets'; 'Does not edit file 08' as 'edits no file-08 cell'; 'No SATISFIED' as 'marks no row SATISFIED'; 'No blueprint' as 'does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/'; and 'Does not coin DESIGN-ACCEPTED' as the broader 'coins no status token'. The only substantive content with no block-one equivalent is the row-name sentence, and that is precisely what clause 3 unions.

The union sentence is verbatim from the deleted block and absent from the kept one, both checked by exact substring against the live register, and its insertion anchor 'This entry marks no row SATISFIED' is present in block one where clause 3 says to place it.

Clause 3's further claim that the sentence is 'already true of the adopted D-056 draft' verifies against the frozen turn-2 subject. Its eligible-in-kind table is exactly DR-102, DR-115, DR-119 and DR-123; its ineligible table contains the named five DR-103, DR-104, DR-105, DR-114 and DR-118; the twelve no-contract rows expand from the draft's shorthand to exactly twelve — DR-101, 107, 111, 112, 117, 120, 121, 122, 124, 125, 126, 127; and the nine deferral-limb rows carry 'Deferral limb of condition 2 (D-002 / D-010)'. So the union adds nothing to D-056 that D-056 did not already decide.

The deletion boundary in clause 2 matches the file's actual structure. Block two is immediately preceded by a horizontal rule — the bytes before its heading are '6.

---

#' — and its final line is '- **Commit:** C-D056.', so 'from the horizontal rule that precedes its heading through its Commit: C-D056. line, inclusive of that rule' describes a well-formed span that leaves block one intact.

The attack 'changes D-056 substance' fails: the header states 'Does not amend D-056's adopted substance', the readiness effect is 'Zero. D-056's readiness effect is unchanged', and the only content movement is a sentence taken from one adopted recital into the other, which I confirmed originates in the adopted draft.

The attack 'adopts the in-flight D-085 SATISFIED draft' fails on three surfaces: the header's 'Does not perform the D-085 SATISFIED re-record draft', clause 4's 'Do not adopt or freeze the in-flight D-085 SATISFIED draft', and the rejected alternative 'Bundle this into D-085. Rejected: D-085 as currently drafted is a SATISFIED re-record, a different act.' D-085 is absent from COORD, so it is genuinely in flight.

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED', 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fail: the header refuses SATISFIED, file-08 edits, the implementation directory and coining a status token; clause 4 repeats all four; the readiness effect keeps 'Condition 2 stays NOT MET. Condition 5 stays last.' file 08 measures unchanged and git reports COORD unmodified in my working tree.

All five measured inputs match live bytes — COORD e6575389…, file 08 ff2ebadd…, the freeze, the D-056 turn-2 subject dfb0c2af… and the D-056 commit 75c981dd…, which resolves to 'D-056: SATISFIED-vs-qualification successor amendment'. Both recital verdict digests also verify: my own D-056 turn-2 verdict at 8a95badb… and the Codex one at 6e755bee…, which I hashed without opening. The entry's claim that both recitals cite the same subject and the same two verdicts is therefore checkable and correct.

The form citation holds: D-073 and D-080 are both present in COORD and ADOPTED, and both are COORD recital corrections, so 'Same class as D-080 / D-073' is apt. D-056 is ADOPTED, and D-087 is not yet in COORD so adoption creates no collision.
Reversibility matches the act in both limbs: 'C-D087 plus restore of the deleted second recital and removal of the union sentence.' Two changes, two restorations.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

The merits of D-056 itself. I reviewed both its turns and consented at turn 2; this entry does not reopen it and I did not re-audit it.
The D-085 draft's contents. It is in flight, this entry refuses to adopt it, and reading it is not needed to verify that refusal.

Whether the cause stated for the duplication — 'two apply writers appended in the same commit window' — is what actually happened. I verified the effect, that two recitals exist and cite identical sources, not the mechanism.

Whether any consumer elsewhere in the corpus cites the second recital by line number or offset and would be disturbed by its removal. I checked that D-056 is the only duplicated heading; I did not sweep for citations into the deleted span.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. The trap in a de-duplication entry is that the two things are not actually duplicates, and here they are not — 2825 bytes against 2406, with each recital holding text the other lacks. I diffed them myself before reading what the entry proposed, so that the row-name sentence was something I had already identified as the deletion's cost rather than something I accepted because clause 3 mentioned it. Every other block-two claim turns out to have a block-one equivalent, usually broader. The keep-the-first reason is verifiable rather than stylistic, the deletion span matches the file's real structure down to the preceding rule and the closing Commit line, and the unioned sentence is true of the adopted draft it came from.
